title: Compact exterior products and properly supported classes
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], writing $A=A_{E,r}$ with $r\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $K,L$ be bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] on their small etale sites, or their specified pro-etale realizations [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Write $K\boxtimes_A^L L=\operatorname{pr}_X^*K\otimes_A^L\operatorname{pr}_Y^*L$, and use the compact-support functors [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. The compact exterior-product map, defined on proper compactifications by the ordinary exterior-product map on extension-by-zero complexes, is an isomorphism
$$\kappa_c:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_c(Y,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X\times_kY,K\boxtimes_A^L L).$$
It is natural in $K,L$. Let $Z\subseteq X$, $W\subseteq Y$ be closed subschemes proper over $k$. Use the supported exterior product [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] and its site comparison [lem-pur-support-site-comparison]. Write $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, and let $C_i\dashv R\Gamma_Z$ be the adjunction of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product], with $C_i(M)=i_*\underline M_Z$ and counit $\epsilon_i:C_i(M)\to K$ for $M=R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$. Since $Z$ is proper over $k$, it is closed in every compactification $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ over $k$, so $j_!i_*=\bar i_*$ for the closed immersion $\bar i:Z\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,i_*\underline M_Z)=R\Gamma(Z,\underline M_Z)$. Define $u_Z:R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\to R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ as the constant-section unit $M\to R\Gamma(Z,\underline M_Z)$ followed by $R\Gamma_c(X,\epsilon_i)$, and define $u_W$ and $u_{Z\times W}$ (for $K\boxtimes_A^L L$ and the proper support $Z\times_kW$) in the same way. On $H^a$, $u_Z$ sends the class of a supported morphism $\alpha:i_*A_Z\to K[a]$ to the compact-support direct image $R\Gamma(Z,A)\to R\Gamma_c(X,K)[a]$ of $\alpha$, precomposed with the constant-section unit $A\to R\Gamma(Z,A)$. These maps satisfy, in $D(A)$,
$$u_{Z\times W}\circ\kappa^{Z,W}=\kappa_c\circ(u_Z\otimes_A^Lu_W).$$
For any open compactification $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ with $\overline X$ proper over $k$, $Z$ is closed in $\overline X$, restriction gives the excision isomorphism $R\Gamma_Z(\overline X,j_\mathrm{ext}K)\cong R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$ whenever $j_\mathrm{ext}K$ is a bounded-below complex on $\overline X$ with a given isomorphism $j^*j_\mathrm{ext}K\cong K$, and the composite
$$R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\xrightarrow{u_Z}R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(\overline X,j_\mathrm{ext}K)$$
is its inverse followed by forgetting support. The second arrow is induced by the map $j_!K\to j_\mathrm{ext}K$ adjoint to that isomorphism. Finally let $K=A(r)_X$ and $L=A(s)_Y$ be coefficient twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], identify $K\boxtimes_A^L L$ with $A(r+s)_{X\times_kY}$ by the twist multiplication, and let $Z\subseteq X$, $W\subseteq Y$ be arbitrary closed subschemes. For classes $\alpha\in H^a_Z(X,A(r))$ and $\beta\in H^b_W(Y,A(s))$ with $a,b$ even, the class $\kappa^{Z,W}(\alpha\otimes\beta)\in H^{a+b}_{Z\times_kW}(X\times_kY,A(r+s))$, transported to the pro-etale site by [lem-pur-support-site-comparison], equals the supported cup product [def-pur-supported-cup] $\operatorname{pr}_X^*\alpha\cup\operatorname{pr}_Y^*\beta$ of the supported pullbacks of [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality]; here $\operatorname{pr}_X^{-1}(Z)\times_{X\times_kY}\operatorname{pr}_Y^{-1}(W)=Z\times_kW$. These assertions and these named maps agree under the finite etale-to-pro-etale comparisons [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison, lem-pur-support-site-comparison].

proof.text: Apply [prop-compactification-refinement] to the separated finite-type maps $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to choose proper compactifications $j_X:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and $j_Y:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ over $k$. Apply [lem-pur-ordinary-kunneth-finite-ring] to the extension-by-zero complexes $j_{X,!}K$ and $j_{Y,!}L$ on the proper compactifications. Its canonical exterior-product isomorphism identifies the tensor of their derived global sections with the derived sections of the tensor on $\overline X\times_k\overline Y$. The compatibility $(j_X\times_kj_Y)_!(K\boxtimes_A^L L)\simeq j_{X,!}K\boxtimes_A^Lj_{Y,!}L$ follows from the defining zero-extension presheaves after sheafification: on geometric stalks both sides are the derived tensor of the two factor stalks, hence are zero off $X\times_kY$ and agree with $K\boxtimes_A^LL$ on that open; K-flat resolutions and exactness of extension by zero make this a derived isomorphism. The definition of the ordinary etale compact-support functor [def-amb-etale-compact-support] then identifies the source and target with $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_c(Y,L)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X\times_kY,K\boxtimes_A^LL)$, respectively. This is precisely $\kappa_c$, and naturality follows from naturality of the Kunneth arrow and compactification comparisons.

Put $M=R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$ and $N=R\Gamma_W(Y,L)$. Because $Z$ and $W$ are proper over $k$, the composites $Z\to X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and $W\to Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ are proper immersions (closed immersion followed by open immersion is an immersion, and the source is proper over $k$); a proper immersion is a closed immersion. The product support is likewise proper and closed. For the closed-support adjunctions $C_i\dashv R\Gamma_Z$ and $C_j\dashv R\Gamma_W$, the maps $u_Z$ and $u_W$ are the units to the compactly supported direct images followed by the counits $C_i(M)\to K$ and $C_j(N)\to L$. The explicit construction of the supported exterior product [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] says that $\kappa^{Z,W}$ is the adjoint of $C_{Z\times W}(M\otimes_A^LN)\to p_X^*C_i(M)\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*C_j(N)\to K\boxtimes_A^LL$. After identifying $R\Gamma_c(X,C_i(M))$ and $R\Gamma_c(Y,C_j(N))$ with $R\Gamma(Z,\underline M_Z)$ and $R\Gamma(W,\underline N_W)$, the two composites in the displayed equation are adjoints of this same morphism, by functoriality of tensor products and of the three counits. Hence $u_{Z\times W}\circ\kappa^{Z,W}=\kappa_c\circ(u_Z\otimes_A^Lu_W)$ in $D(A)$. Taking cohomology gives the stated description of $u_Z$ on a supported morphism.

proof.text: Let $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be any open compactification and let $j_{\mathrm{ext}}K$ be a bounded-below extension with $j^*j_{\mathrm{ext}}K\cong K$. Excision for sections with support is the standard cone calculation: the support complex is the cone of restriction to the open complement, equivalently the cone description of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], and restriction along the open neighbourhood $X$ of $Z$ identifies the two cones. Thus $R\Gamma_Z(\overline X,j_{\mathrm{ext}}K)\cong R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$. Since $Z$ is closed in $\overline X$, the extension-by-zero map $j_!K\to j_{\mathrm{ext}}K$ induces the second arrow $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\to R\Gamma(\overline X,j_{\mathrm{ext}}K)$. Under the excision identification, the composite from $R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$ through $u_Z$ and this arrow is exactly the map obtained by forgetting support, so it is the claimed inverse followed by forgetting support. All identifications are natural in the extension and in $K$.

source.place: Step 1: compatibility with forgetting support in the compactification

proof.text: For $K=A(r)_X$ and $L=A(s)_Y$, the twist multiplication from [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] identifies $K\boxtimes_A^LL$ with $A(r+s)_{X\times_kY}$. Represent $\alpha$ and $\beta$ by the supported morphisms used in [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]. The definition of the supported cup product [def-pur-supported-cup] is the same adjoint composite as the definition of $\kappa^{Z,W}$, followed by the shift comparison and this twist multiplication; therefore $\kappa^{Z,W}(\alpha\otimes\beta)$ is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*\alpha\cup\operatorname{pr}_Y^*\beta$. The pullback and cup compatibilities, including the even-degree sign, are exactly [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality]. For pro-etale realizations, [lem-pur-support-site-comparison] gives the equality of the supported exterior-product maps under the canonical tensor comparison, while [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] gives the corresponding comparison for compact-support direct images. Combining these natural comparison squares proves the final agreement clause for all stated witnesses and supports.
